questions.question: A fraction (3)/(5)is decreased by (2)/(5). The resulting fraction is then increased by 20%. What is the percentage decrease/increase in the value of the original fraction?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A fraction dfrac{3}{5} is decreased by dfrac{2}{5}. The resulting fraction is then increased by 20%.

**Formula used:**

New Value = Original Value × (1 + Percentage Change)

**Calculation:**

Initial Fraction = dfrac{3}{5}

Decreased Fraction: dfrac{3}{5} - dfrac{2}{5} = dfrac{1}{5}

Increased by 20%: dfrac{1}{5} times (1 + 0.20) = dfrac{1}{5} times 1.20

⇒ dfrac{1}{5} times 1.20 = dfrac{1.20}{5} = dfrac{6}{25}

Percentage Change = dfrac{dfrac{6}{25} - dfrac{3}{5}}{dfrac{3}{5}} times 100\%

⇒ dfrac{dfrac{6}{25} - dfrac{15}{25}}{dfrac{3}{5}} times 100\%

⇒ dfrac{-9}{25} times dfrac{5}{3} times 100 %

⇒ -60\%

**∴ The correct answer is option 3 i.e. decrease by 60%.**

questions.question: Of the two numbers, 28% of the first is equal to 64% of the second. What is the ratio of the first and second number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If x% of the first number = y% of the second number, the ratio of the first to the second is directly y : x.

First Number : Second Number = 64 : 28

⇒ First Number : Second Number = 16 : 7

**∴ The correct answer is 16 : 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d7baac48c702c663056fca8722f7633954872dec75022fac266ce10b56c24db2.png] 

**Given:**

28% of the first number = 64% of the second number

**Calculations:**

Let the first number be A and the second number be B.

⇒ 28% of A = 64% of B

⇒ (28 ÷ 100) × A = (64 ÷ 100) × B

⇒ 28 × A = 64 × B

⇒ A ÷ B = 64 ÷ 28

Dividing numerator and denominator by their highest common factor (4):

⇒ A ÷ B = 16 ÷ 7

⇒ A : B = 16 : 7

**∴ The correct answer is 16 : 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage to Ratio Conversion

If a% of x = b% of y, then the ratio of x to y is strictly the inverse ratio of their percentages, which directly means x : y = b : a.

Properties of Proportions

If a : b = c : d, then a × d = b × c. This fundamental rule states that the product of the extremes equals the product of the means.

Simplifying Ratios

A ratio a : b is in its simplest form when the highest common factor (HCF) of a and b is exactly 1. In the given question, 64 and 28 are divided by their HCF, which is 4.

questions.question: The present ages of a mother and her son are in the ratio of 6 : 1. When the son becomes as old as his mother now, then the ratio of his father's age to his mother's age is 13 : 11. When the son becomes as old as his father now, then the sum of the ages of the father and son will be 115 years. The present age of the father is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The present ages of a mother and her son are in the ratio of 6 : 1

When the son becomes as old as his mother now, then the ratio of his father's age to his mother's age is 13 : 11

When the son becomes as old as his father now, then the sum of the ages of the father and son will be 115 years

**Calculation:**

Let the present age of mother and son be 6x and x

and father's age be y

Now,

According to the question,

After 5x years

Mother = 6x + 5x = 11x 

Father = y + 5x

Now

y + 5x/11x = 13/11

⇒ y = 8x

So, the father's age is 8x years

Again,

After 7x years

Father = 8x + 7x = 15x

Son = x + 7x = 8x

15x + 8x = 115 years

23x = 115 years

x = 115/23 = 5 years

So the age of the father is 8 × 5 = 40 years

**∴ The present age of the father is 40 years**

questions.question: A cylinder has radius of 6 cm and height equal to 7 cm. A hemisphere has radius of 9 cm. Height of a cone is 12 cm and radius of its base is 8 cm. What is the ratio of volumes of cylinder, hemisphere and cone?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of the Cylinder = 6 cm

Height of the Cylinder h = 7cm

Radius of hemisphere = 9 cm

Height(h) of the cone = 12 cm

Radius(r) of the cone = 8 cm

**Formula used:**

Volume of the Cylinder = pi r²h 

Volume of hemisphere = dfrac{2}{3}pi r³

Volume(V) of a cone = dfrac{1}{3}pi r²h

**Calculation:**

Volume of the Cylinder = pi r²h 

⇒π× 6² × 7

⇒ 252 π

Volume of hemisphere = dfrac{2}{3}pi r³

⇒ (2/3) ×π × 9 × 9 × 9

⇒ 486 π

Volume(V) of a cone = dfrac{1}{3}pi r²h

⇒ (1/3) ×π × 8 × 8 × 12

⇒ 256 π

Ratio of volumes of cylinder, hemisphere and cone

⇒ 252 π : 486 π : 256 π

⇒ 126 : 243 : 128

∴ Ratio of volumes of cylinder, hemisphere and cone is 126 : 243 : 128.

questions.question: In what ratio does the point P(7, 3) divide the line segment joining A(4, -3) and B(9, 7)?
questions.solution:
Given:

Points A(4, -3), B(9, 7) and P(7, 3)

Formula Used:

If a point (x, y) divides a line segment in ratio m : n whose endpoints are (x1, y1) and (x2, y2),

Then the y-coordinates of that point are dfrac{my₂ + ny₁}{m+n}.

Calculation:

Using the above formulae,

We have x1 = 4, y1 = - 3, x2 = 9, y2 = 7

The coordinates of the point of division are (7, 3).

On comparing the y-coordinate we have,

dfrac{7m + (-3)n}{m+n} = 3

⇒ 7m - 3n = 3m + 3n

⇒ 7m - 3m = 3n + 3n

⇒ 4m = 6n

⇒ dfrac{m}{n} = dfrac{6}{4} = dfrac{3}{2}

**∴ Required ratio = 3 : 2.**

questions.question: In a class of 60 students, 40% are girls. The average weight of the whole class is 59.2 and the average weight of the girls is 55 kg. What is the average weight of the boys?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total number of students in the class = 60

Number of girls in the class = 40%

The average weight of the whole class = 59.2

The average weight of the girls = 55 kg

**Concept used:**

Average = sum of observations/Number of observations

**Calculation:**

Sum of weight of all class = (59.2 × 60) = 3552

Number of girls in the class = (60 × (40)/({100)}) = 24

Number of boys in the class = (60 - 24) = 36

Sum of weight of girls = (55 × 24) = 1320

Sum of weight of boys = (3552 - 1320) = 2232

Average weight of boys = ((2232)/({36)}) = **62 kg**

**∴ The average weight of the boys is 62 kg.**

questions.question: A bag contains 3 red marbles, 4 blue marbles, and 5 green marbles. If two marbles are randomly selected from the bag with replacement, what is the probability that the two marbles are the same color?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **25/72.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Replacement is an important factor in the calculation of this problem.
 
• The probability of selecting two marbles of the same color with replacement is 25/72
 
• The probability can be calculated by multiplying the individual probabilities of selecting the same color marble twice.
 
• The formula for this is P(same color) = (P(color1))² + (P(color2))2+ (P(color3))2
 
• The number of possible outcomes is calculated by multiplying the total number of marbles in the bag by the number of selections.
 
• The number of favorable outcomes is calculated by multiplying the number of marbles of the same color by itself.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The probability of selecting two marbles of the same color with replacement can also be calculated by multiplying the probability of selecting one marble of a certain color by itself.
 
• The formula for this is P(same color) = (P(color1))² + (P(color2))² + (P(color3))²
 
• In this question, P(same color) = (3/12)² + (4/12)² + (5/12)² = 25/72

questions.question: The area of the sector of a circle of radius 12 cm is 32 π cm² Find the length of the corresponding arc of the sector.
questions.solution:

The area of a sector of a circle = 32 π cm²

Radius of circle (R) = 12 cm

**Formula used:**

Area of a sector = (π × R² × θ)/360

Lenght of an arc = (2 × π × R × θ)/360

**Calculation:**

Area of a sector = (π × R2 × θ)/360

⇒ 32π = (π × (12)2 × θ)/360

⇒ 32 × 360 = (144 × θ)

⇒ θ = (32 × 360)/144

⇒ θ = 80° 

Lenght of an arc = (2 × π × R × θ)/360

⇒ (2 × π × 12 × 80)/360

⇒ (16/3) × π

**∴ The correct answer is ​​(16)/(3) π cm.**

Find the greatest number that will divide 57, 93 and 191 so as to leave the same remainder in each case.
questions.solution:
**Given**

Numbers: 57, 93, 191

**Concept:**

The greatest number that leaves the same remainder when dividing multiple numbers is the greatest common divisor (GCD) of the differences between those numbers.

**Calculation:**

Find the differences between the numbers ⇒ 93 - 57 = 36, 191 - 93 = 98

The GCD of 36 and 98 is 2

**Therefore, the greatest number that will divide 57, 93 and 191 so as to leave the same remainder in each case is 2.**

questions.question: Avra travels from A to B at 74 km/h and returns from B to A through the same route at 111 km/h. What was his average speed during the two-way journey?
questions.solution:
**Given:** 

Avra travels from A to B at 74 km/h and returns from B to A through the same route at 111 km/h

Formula used:

Average Speed = 2ab/(a + b)

__
 
• Applicable when one travels at speed a for half the distance and speed b for the other half of the distance.
 
• In this case, the average speed is the harmonic mean of the two speeds. On similar lines, you can modify this formula for one-third distance.

 

Calculation:

According to the concept,

Average speed = (2 × 74 × 111)/(111 + 74)

⇒ 16428/185

⇒ 88.8

**∴ Average speed of the Avra is 88.8 km/h**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

1. Average Speed = (a + b)/2

 
• Applicable when one travels at speed a for half the time and speed b for another half of the time.
 
• In this case, the average speed is the arithmetic mean of the two speeds.

2. Average Speed = 3abc/(ab + bc + ca)

 
• Applicable when one travels at speed a for one-third of the distance, at speed b for another one-third of the distance and speed c for rest of the one-third of the distance.

questions.question: One third part of a certain journey is covered at the speed of 18 km/hr, one fourth part at the speed of 27 km/hr and the rest part at the speed of 45 km/hr. What will be the average speed for the whole journey?
questions.solution:
Given: 

1/3 part of journey is covered at the speed of = 18 km/h

1/4 part of journey is covered at the speed of = 27 km/h

And the remaining part of journey at the speed of = 45 km/h

Formula used:

Average Speed = Total Distance/Total Time

Calculation: 

Let the total distance be S km

According to the question,

First part = S/3, 

Time taken = (S/3)/18 = S/54

Second part = S/4

Time taken = (S/4)/27 = S/108

Remaining part = S - (S/3 + S/4) = 5S/12

Time taken = (5S/12)/45 = S/108

Total time = S/54 + S/108 + S/108 = 4S/108 = S/27

The Average speed = Total distance/Total time

Average Speed = S/(S/27) = 27

**∴ The average speed of the whole journey will be 27 km/hr**
